title: Practice 11: за and под: going behind, under

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Сталь закаляется за ___ (одна секунда, acc. sg.).
exercises.why: **секунда → секунду** (acc. sg.). Feminine, nominative singular in -а. Declines like DLI's газета — every singular form has the same endings (A. sg. газету). Ending -а → -у.  **один → одну** (acc. sg. f., agreeing with секунду). «один» is a pronoun-type word with its own declension, not the regular adjective pattern, so no ending rule is claimed. Its forms (f. sg.): одна · одной · одной · одну · одной · одной.  Declension: sg. секунда · секунды · секунде · секунду · секундой · секунде; pl. секунды · секунд · секундам · секунды · секундами · секундах.  «The accusative singular of all feminine nouns ending in -ь is the same as nominative. The accusative singular of all other feminine nouns ends in -у or -ю.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

**подушка → подушку** (acc. sg.). Feminine, nominative singular in -а. Declines like DLI's газета — every singular form has the same endings (A. sg. газету). Ending -а → -у.  **нижний → нижнюю** (acc. sg. f., agreeing with подушку). Adjective type II, soft — declines like DLI's синий (every form has the same endings): A. синюю. Ending -яя → -юю.  Declension: sg. подушка · подушки · подушке · подушку · подушкой · подушке; pl. подушки · подушек · подушкам · подушки · подушками · подушках.  «The accusative singular of all feminine nouns ending in -ь is the same as nominative. The accusative singular of all other feminine nouns ends in -у or -ю.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  Adjectives in the accusative: animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative (masculine and plural); feminine -ую, -юю. — DLI, Lessons 46–47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Твоё сердце омрачилось за ___ (прошедший, acc. pl.) годы.

No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative. exercises.q: Под ___ (какой омёт, acc. pl.) не закапывайте зерно, мы везде сыщем.
exercises.why: **омёт → ометы** (acc. pl.). Masculine, inanimate; nominative plural омёты. Declines like DLI's стол — every plural form has the same endings (A. pl. столы). Ending — (no ending) → -ы.  **какой → какие** (acc. pl., agreeing with ометы). Adjective type III, guttural (after г, к, х) — declines like DLI's русский (every form has the same endings, apart from the masculine nominative singular (and the inanimate accusative equal to it), which ends in -ой here, not -ий): A. anim. = G., inan. = N. No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  Declension: sg. омёт · омёта · омёту · омёт · омётом · омёте; pl. омёты · омётов · омётам · омёты · омётами · омётах.  «The accusative plural of inanimate nouns is the same as the nominative plural. The accusative plural of animate nouns is the same as the genitive plural.» — DLI, Lesson 42.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Masculine adjectives of the "hard" and "guttural" types have in the nominative the ending -ой if stressed: новый — молодой; русский — плохой, and retain the stress on the ending throughout the declension.» «The adjective «большой» belongs to the guttural type, in spite of its -ш-: большого, большому, большим, о большом.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Notice that the adjectives of the "soft", "guttural" and "sibilant" types are declined in the plural in the very same way.» — DLI, Lesson 48.  Adjectives in the accusative: animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative (masculine and plural); feminine -ую, -юю. — DLI, Lessons 46–47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).
